selected.title: A 1,500-year-old clay figure may show a woman guarding a tomb
selected.summary: Archaeologists found a carefully detailed haniwa figure at a fifth-century burial mound in Gunma, Japan. Experts think it may depict a miko, a female ritual figure.
selected.why_it_matters: The figure offers a vivid glimpse of funeral practices and the ceremonial roles women may have held in ancient Japan.
selected.challenge_question: What is the ancient Japanese clay figure thought to represent?
selected.answer_explanation: Its hairstyle, bracelets, sash and ritual implement led experts to suggest it represents a miko, a female ritual figure. The identification is an interpretation, not a confirmed identity.
selected.butterfly_question: What can objects buried with the dead reveal about who held influence in ancient societies?
